9 Best Things to Do in Marrakesh 🕌✨ 1) Stay in a Riad 🛏️  feel the authentic Moroccan vibe, from the mosaic tiles to the whisper-quiet courtyards. Riads offer privacy, fewer crowds, and a home-away-from-home feel with traditional decor, often a peaceful rooftop terrace, and staff who treat you like family. Perfect for a truly Moroccan experience without the hotel hustle. 2) Best Coffee at Bacha Coffee ☕️✨ (Location: https://goo.gl/maps/6u3Xx9J9xqv1w9Qw7) Silky espresso, perfectly balanced blends, and a chic, relaxed atmosphere. Great latte art, friendly baristas, and a bright, stylish space to post your vibes. Pro tip: try their signature crush coffee and pastry pairing. 3) Explore the Souks 🧿🌀 Fun tip: haggle with a smile, never agree to the first price! Make it a playful game, sample spices, and test your bargaining skills. Lose yourself in ribbons of color, leather, pottery, and lamps. The thrill of the find is half the fun! 4) Visit Ben Youssef Madrasa 🕌 A jaw-dropping historic site with intricate tilework, carved wood, and serene courtyards. It’s a perfect spot for photos that scream old-world Marrakech charm. 5) Jardin Majorelle 🌿💙 iconic cobalt-blue paths, lush botanical displays, and a peaceful escape from the market buzz. A must-see for color lovers and plant enthusiasts, plus it’s connected to the Yves Saint Laurent legacy. 6) Ourika Valley Day Trip 🚙🌄 about 1 hour from central Marrakech (depending on traffic). What to expect: stunning valley scenery, Berber villages, waterfalls, and a cooler climate. A refreshing break from the medina with photo-worthy viewpoints. 7) Agafay Desert Experience 🐫🏜️ Highlights: camel ride under the open sky, squad  bike moments, and magical desert views. Luxe touch: stay at a desert camp with plush lounges, gourmet meals, and starlit dinners. Perfect for a memorable  outing. 8) Dinner at La Trattoria 🍝🇮🇹  warm, cozy ambiance with authentic Italian flavors in Marrakech. Great for a relaxed evening, fresh pastas, and a lively dining vibe after a day of exploration. 9) Jemaa el-Fnaa - The Heart of Marrakech 🎭💃 Do it for the vibes: bustling square, street performances, snake charmers, and a feast for the senses. Pro tip: bring some cash for photos with performers and for quick bites. Best times: late afternoon into evening when the energy peaks. #Marrakesh #Morocco #TravelTikTok #Riads #Souks

¿Planeando una escapada a Marrakech? ¡Guarda este post porque lo vas a necesitar! 📌 Si tienes pensado visitar Marruecos pronto, te prometo que estas 5 actividades van a hacer que tu viaje pase de ser "muy chulo" a ser INOLVIDABLE. ✨ Aquí te dejo el resumen de mi top definitivo para que lo tengas a mano: 🎬 5. Ait Ben Haddou: Una excursión obligatoria. Pasear por esta ciudad de barro amurallada es sentirte dentro de Gladiator o Juego de Tronos. ¡Súper fotogénico! 🕌 4. Perderte con un guía local: La Medina es un laberinto increíble. Ir con alguien de allí es la mejor forma de empaparte de su cultura y descubrir joyas como el Palacio de la Bahía. 🎈 3. Vuelo en globo al amanecer: Madrugar nunca mereció tanto la pena. Ver salir el sol desde las alturas y rematar con un desayuno tradicional... una locura. 🌊 2. Cascadas de Ouzoud: Un contraste total de naturaleza pura. Si vas temprano podrás disfrutar de un paseo en barca espectacular y saludar a los monos que viven allí. 🐒 🐫 1. Atardecer y noche en el desierto: Adrenalina pura en quad, paseo en dromedario y terminar cenando bajo las estrellas. ¡Mi actividad favorita de todo el viaje, un 10/10 en calidad-precio! ¿Cuál de estas 5 tienes más ganas de hacer? ¡Te leo en los comentarios! 👇 Y si tienes cualquier duda sobre cómo reservarlas, pregúntame sin problema. #viajes #marrakech #morocco #viajar #planes

Between 1921 and 1927, #Spanish colonial forces dropped tons of toxic mustard gas across Rif (Northern #morocco ) They deliberately targeted my tribe (Riffians)  and agricultural land.  Northern Morocco still accounts for anoverwhelmingly high percentage of the country’s cancer cases, forcing families to carry the heavy weight of a war that ended a century ago. Historical crimes don’t just stay trapped inside history books. They live on in our bodies, our health, and our daily reality. Planning a trip to Morocco? 🇲🇦 SAVE this for later! Here are 7 things you should know before you go: 1️⃣ Haggling & Shopping — Don’t buy the first thing you see. Shop around, compare prices, and negotiate. 2️⃣ Tourist Pricing — Be mindful of how you identify yourself and where you’re from, as tourist prices can be higher. 3️⃣ Be Comfortable Saying NO — If you show interest in something, sellers may really try to make the sale. Be polite, but be firm. 4️⃣ Make Restaurant Reservations — Popular restaurants can book up, so reserve ahead of time if there’s somewhere you really want to visit. 5️⃣ Know How Taxis Work — Understand the pricing and meter system before getting in. 6️⃣ Explore Beyond Marrakech — You can experience a lot of Marrakech in 3–4 days, so use extra time to explore other parts of Morocco. 7️⃣ Agafay ≠ The Sahara — Agafay is beautiful, but it’s not the same as experiencing the iconic Sahara sand dunes. If you have the time, consider an overnight Sahara trip. Morocco is an incredible country, but knowing these things BEFORE you go can make your trip so much smoother. 🇲🇦✨ Save this for your Morocco trip and send it to your travel buddy! ✈️🐪 #traveltips #travelguide #travelcreator #moroccotravel #travelinspiration
